title: Sneaking in to hear Bert Williams and Black Patti
summary: At nine he sneaked into the opera house for Bert Williams; Mrs. Howard recalls seeing the singer Sissieretta Jones, called Black Patti, in Steubenville.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh. Okay. Well, I didn't know that 'cause we didn't have that down anywhere. In the article here, it says that you remembered--you told the interviewer that when you were nine years old, you sneaked into the opera house in order to listen to Bert Williams.
I did.
So was that right?

Sneaked in the opera house to listen to Bert Williams, and then they had--what's that other girl's name? Susie know, and I can't think of that lady's name--with the knowledge. She was a--Mama, what was the name of that other lady in the opera house?
Oh, Black Patty?
Yeah, Black Patty.
That was a singer, Black Patty?
Uh-huh. Yeah. You done heard 'er? Hear anything of her?
(laughter) huh, she was good.
So you've heard of her?
No, I haven't. Now I have.
She was what you would call a coloratura.
Coloratura?
Yeah.
Yeah.
Oh.
Black Patty? That's all her name was?
Her first name was Sissinetta Jones.
Uh-huh.
But they gave her that name, I believe, over in Europe. (inaudible)
Her name was Cis--
What was her real name again?
Cissarella (phonetic) Jones.
Sister Etta Jones?
Cissaretta (phonetic).
Oh, Cissaretta. Do you know how to spell that?
I think it was the way they spelled it -- S-i-s-r-e-t-t-a -- Sisretta.
Sisretta Jones. And then you say she toured Europe, they gave her the nickname Black Patty?
Yeah, I think that's the way. (inaudible).
Would you know about what year that was that she was touring, or--
It was, oh--
--Her career?

Oh, now I remember the first time that I saw her. See, I was born in Atlanta. And the first time I saw her I think I was around 11 or 12 years old. --oh, her career-- And (inaudible) let's see, I think she had traveled all round -- round 1927 -- it was in the 1920s actually. But, oh -- at that time, she was the world's best.
It's wonderful to know that.
Uh-huh.
Where did you see her?
Huh?
Where was it that you saw her?
In Atlanta, Georgia.
You saw her in Atlanta? And you saw her in--was it in Steubenville?
Yeah, Steubenville.
Huh. So she toured the whole country?
(inaudible)
And Europe.

(inaudible) Steubenville. And they went from Pittsburgh to see all the big shows--they would play Pittsburgh. Then they'd go to Steubenville--it's kinda off--I don't know (inaudible). But that's the way it was. And they would play--I think Irene told me --would play, was it a week stand, Babe?
Paul, was it a week stand?
Yeah.
That the big shows--
--Week stand.
They'd play one week stand in Steubenville?
Uh-huh.
I think that was to cut a--you know, a route or something--I don't know what. A layover or something.
Yeah, to cut a layover.
What do you remember about Bert
(inaudible) About what?
--About Bert Williams' performance?
When you sneaked into opera house when you were a boy to see him? What do you remember about the performance?
All I know, I went there to see him. He sho' was worth seein'.
Did you enjoy yourself?
Oh, yeah, sure I enjoyed myself.
A thrill for a nine-year-old--for anybody--for a nine-year-old kid--
Yep. It was quite a thrill.
What did you think of him?
Huh?
What did you think of him?
I thought he was the greatest. Singin' and dancin' and everything.
Do you remember anything about his performance? About how he danced, or what he sang, or what really impressed you most?
Oh, what the people would say about him. I was too young--I was too young to get all them things together.
Did you get to see any other entertainers of the time that might've come to--?
(End of Side 1)
